original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g, h ∈ L∞(µ). If C(n) := ∫ f · T^n g · T^(2n) h dµ, is the sequence (C(n)) an approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Special Case of Problem 1 (the special case of Problem 1 on the structure of multiple correlation sequences): whether the sequence C(n):=∫_X f·T^n g·T^{2n}h dμ is an (approximate) integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct special case from the paper: one transformation T, three functions f,g,h∈L∞(μ), the correlation sequence C(n)=∫_X f·T^n g·T^{2n}h dμ, and the target class of generalized 2-step nilsequences. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: The official formulation asks whether C is an "(approximate) integral combination" of generalized 2-step nilsequences, not only whether it is an approximate integral combination; your draft drops the exact-integral-combination option that the paper explicitly leaves open. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The paper’s ambient object is an invertible measure-preserving system on a probability space; in the draft, invertibility and measure-preservation are left implicit in the word "system." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

To be stand-alone, the question should define what a generalized 2-step nilsequence is: a uniform limit of basic generalized 2-step nilsequences, where in the basic model the test function on the 2-step nilmanifold is allowed to be Riemann-integrable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

To be stand-alone, the question should define "integral combination": representation via a compact metric parameter space M, a complex Borel measure of bounded variation σ on M, and a σ-integrable family of generalized 2-step nilsequences ψ_m with C(n)=∫_M ψ_m(n)dσ(m). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
It should also define "approximate" precisely: for every ε>0, one can write C=C_ε+e_ε where C_ε is such an integral combination and ‖e_ε‖∞<ε. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The special case in the updated paper does not assume ergodicity, even though the nearby discussion immediately recalls an ergodic decomposition theorem C(n)=N(n)+e(n) with e small only in density; that distinction is worth making explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

The draft does not specify the indexing set of the sequence or that this is the one-variable instance of the paper’s more general multicorrelation-sequence problem. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let (X,𝓧,μ,T) be an invertible measure-preserving system on a probability space, and let f,g,h∈L∞(μ). Define the one-variable correlation sequence C=(C(n)) by C(n):=∫_X f·T^n g·T^{2n}h dμ. Is C an (approximate) integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences, in the following sense: does there exist either an exact representation of C, or for every ε>0 a sequence C_ε with ‖C-C_ε‖∞<ε, such that C_ε(n)=∫_M ψ_m(n)dσ(m) for some compact metric space M, some complex Borel measure σ of bounded variation on M, and some family {ψ_m}_{m∈M} of generalized 2-step nilsequences with m↦ψ_m(n) σ-integrable for each n; here a generalized 2-step nilsequence means a uniform limit of basic sequences n↦F(a^n x) arising from a 2-step nilmanifold G/Γ with a∈G, x∈G/Γ, and F Riemann-integrable? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
justification: The draft is aiming at the updated arXiv-v3 Special Case of Problem 1 in §4.1, not at a broader neighboring problem. The paper first introduces generalized nilsequences in §2.4.2, then defines "integral combination" and "approximate integral combination" in §4.1, and immediately after that states this exact special case for C(n)=∫ f·T^n g·T^{2n}h dμ. The nearby discussion explains why the question is posed in this sharper form: known results only give a decomposition into a 2-step nilsequence plus an error term small in density, which is insufficient for sparse subsequences. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
